name: Lake District
title: Holidays in the Lake District
intro: England's biggest national park, with sixteen lakes, its highest mountains, lake steamers and the landscapes that inspired Wordsworth and Beatrix Potter. Here's what the Lake District is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: A wooden boathouse on the shore of Ullswater in the Lake District, with wooded hills reflected in the lake

facts.label: Entry
facts.value: No passport checks within the UK

facts_note: UK and Irish citizens don't need a passport to travel within the UK, but airlines ask for photo ID. Most other visitors need an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA), so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June and September are the best months, with the driest weather of the year and long days for walking. July and August are the warmest but the roads and car parks around Windermere, Ambleside and Keswick get busy. October brings autumn colour. Winter is cold and wet, with snow on the high fells, but cosy pubs and empty paths. It rains a lot here in every season, so bring waterproofs.

things.name: Windermere lake cruise
things.blurb: Steamers and launches link Lakeside, Bowness and Ambleside on England's longest lake.

things.name: Catbells
things.blurb: A short, steep family favourite above Derwentwater, with views over Keswick from the top.

things.name: Ullswater 'Steamers'
things.blurb: Take the boat to Howtown or Glenridding and walk back along the shore, or visit Aira Force waterfall.

things.name: World of Beatrix Potter
things.blurb: Peter Rabbit and friends in Bowness, with Hill Top, her farmhouse, a short drive away.

things.name: Grasmere
things.blurb: Wordsworth's village, with Dove Cottage and the famous Grasmere gingerbread shop.

things.name: Scafell Pike
things.blurb: England's highest mountain, a full day's hike from Wasdale for fit walkers.

faqs.question: Where is the best place to stay in the Lake District?
faqs.answer: Keswick and Ambleside are good bases with shops, pubs and walks from the door. Bowness and Windermere have the most hotels and lake cruises. Coniston, Grasmere and Ullswater are quieter.

faqs.question: Do you need a car in the Lake District?
faqs.answer: It helps, but you can manage without one. Trains run to Windermere and Penrith, and buses and boats link the main towns in summer.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in the Lake District?
faqs.answer: A long weekend is enough for a taste, but a week lets you explore several lakes and fit walks around the weather.

faqs.question: What is the nearest airport to the Lake District?
faqs.answer: Manchester is about two hours' drive away. Trains run from Manchester Airport to Windermere, changing at Oxenholme.
